description: ARGUS hit this live during Arc 73 design critique: the save-verdict module canonical printf/heredoc form (cat <<EOF ... or the printf redirect) repeatedly failed under this environment Bash-tool command wrapping with an apostrophe-in-heredoc parse error. ARGUS fell back to per-block double-quoted printf redirection (within its Bash grant) which produced an integrity-verified, bw-attached verdict — so it did NOT block. PLAN/next-step: reproduce the failing invocation on Windows git-bash via the Bash tool; determine whether the fix is (a) the save-verdict module switching its canonical write form to per-block double-quoted printf, or (b) a documented Windows-path quoting note in save-verdict.md; decide against the Arc-71 decision-register single-quote-positional precedent. Recurrence risk: every verdict-producing CAPTAIN (ARGUS/VERA/CATO/NOMOS) hits the same write path. Anchor: Arc 73 / stoa--51k.

comments.text: Facet 2 (surfaced Arc 73 close, FM + NOMOS both classified BENIGN): save-verdict on-disk sha vs bw-reported sha mismatch. VERA bw comment claimed verdict sha a2e2b068 but on-disk vera-build.md computed to 30eb13ea. Investigated by FM + NOMOS independently: the file is a COMPLETE genuine VERA PASS verdict verifying the correct build (1d9faa3), content-consistent with its bw summary -- the sha was reported PRE-attach-footer (save-verdict appends an attach footer after computing/reporting the sha, so the reported sha no longer matches the final on-disk bytes). Affected only VERA this arc, not ARGUS/CATO. PLAN: when save-verdict appends a post-write footer (attach metadata), it must EITHER compute+report the sha AFTER the final write, OR not mutate the file after the reported sha. Decide alongside facet-1 (heredoc) as one save-verdict-module pass. Non-blocking; no deliverable impact. [from: PLINY_the-stoa | sid 8da07e98-b189-4669-8626-b37779ad94f0]
